s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, purpuric skin lesion with multifocal peripheral patches, papules, and macules
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Central ulceration and bleeding of the lesion
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Lesion first developed in March 2014
Rapid growth and extension of the lesion in June 2014
Lesion size: 30 × 25-cm
Location of the lesion: left anterior scalp, left parietal scalp, left forehead, left lateral cheek, right frontal scalp, and right parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and ulceration of the purpuric lesion, strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors, and cells staining positively with CD31

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric patches, papules, and macules, and the presence of slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes in the dermis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multifocal peripheral patches, papules, and macules, and the presence of hyperchromatic nuclei in the cells

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesion with rapid growth and extension, and the presence of pale eosinophilic cytoplasm in the cells

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive, ulcerative skin lesion with multifocal peripheral patches, papules, and macules, and the presence of hyperchromatic nuclei in the cells

raw.rationale: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes in the dermis, cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, and strong immunopositivity for CD31 are characteristic features of angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Kaposi's sarcoma can present with similar vascular lesions, the lack of human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) mention and the specific immunohistochemical profile provided do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathological features, including the presence of slitlike spaces and CD31 positivity, do not align with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, which typically involves atypical lymphocytes and different immunophenotyping.

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The description of the lesion and the immunohistochemical findings do not support a diagnosis of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma, which would typically involve B-cell markers and different clinical presentations.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by different clinical and histological features, including epidermal involvement and specific immunophenotyping, which are not described in this case.
